bull.b: Cloudflare has sustained rapid revenue expansion while scaling from $656 million in 2021 to $2.73 billion on a TTM basis. Management’s 37% full-year 2026 growth outlook indicates continued demand for its integrated security, performance, and developer platform services.

Cloudflare is producing substantial operating and free cash flow despite reported GAAP losses, demonstrating that customer subscriptions and usage generate real cash. This supports continued network investment, product development, and balance-sheet management as the business expands.

A 122% dollar-based net retention rate shows existing customers are expanding their Cloudflare spending over time. Broad-based expansion across the portfolio supports recurring revenue durability, improves customer lifetime value, and validates the company’s cross-sell and upsell model.

bear.b: The sharp increase in debt has materially raised financial risk relative to the company’s equity base. Until profitability becomes consistently positive, higher leverage can reduce flexibility for investment, acquisitions, and resilience against weaker operating performance.

Cloudflare’s improving results have not yet translated into sustained GAAP profitability, with operating and net losses continuing across the periods provided. This leaves earnings power less proven and makes the business more dependent on successful cost control and execution.

Declining gross margin can limit the amount of revenue growth that converts into operating profit, particularly as lower-margin compute and usage-based services expand. Although management remains within its target range, continued compression would weaken the long-term scalability of the model.
